# Problem 1
Load a dataset into R, gate it however you like, and then export out a population of interest as their own .fcs files. Open them in either Floreada.io or the commercial software of your choice, and take a screenshot of how they look by two markers of interest.

```{r}
# Load required pacakges
library(flowWorkspace)
library(flowGate)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(purrr)
library(ggcyto)

# Load dataset
Folder <- file.path("data/homework")
fcs_files <- list.files(Folder, pattern = ".fcs", full.names = TRUE)
cytoset <- load_cytoset_from_fcs(fcs_files, truncate_max_range = FALSE, transformation = FALSE)
gatingset <- GatingSet(cytoset)

# Biexponential transformation
Parameters <- colnames(gatingset)
FluorophoresOnly <- Parameters[!stringr::str_detect(Parameters, "FSC|SSC|TIME|-H|-W")]

Biexponential <- flowjo_biexp_trans(channelRange=4096, maxValue=262144, pos=1, neg=4.5, widthBasis=-500)
MyBiexTransform <- transformerList(FluorophoresOnly, Biexponential)
flowWorkspace::transform(gatingset, MyBiexTransform)

# Check transformation
ggcyto(gatingset[2], subset="root",
 aes( x="AF700-A", y="LiveDeadFixableBlue-A")) + geom_hex(bins=150)

# Add gating
GatingTable <- tibble::tribble(
  ~filterId,    ~dims,                          ~subset,              
  "cells",      list("FSC-A", "SSC-A"),          "root",              
  "singlets",   list("FSC-A", "FSC-H"),          "cells",             
  "live",       list("FSC-A", "LiveDeadFixableBlue-A"), "singlets",   
  "Tcells",     list("FSC-A", "AF700-A"),             "live",             
  "CD3-",       list("FSC-A", "AF700-A"),             "live",             
  "Bcells",     list("SparkNIR-685-A", "AF700-A"),              "CD3-",             
  "Bcells+",    list("PE-AF610-A", "FITC-A"),             "Bcells",           
  "CD4+",       list("APC-Fire750-A", "[RY775]-A"),              "Tcells",            
  "CD8+",       list("APC-Fire750-A", "[RY775]-A"),              "Tcells",            
  "DN",         list("APC-Fire750-A", "[RY775]-A"),              "Tcells",            
  "Monocytes",  list("FSC-A", "BUV395-A"),         "live",              
  "Mono+",      list("BV570-A", "SparkBlue-550-A"),            "Monocytes",         
)

flowGate::gs_apply_gating_strategy(gatingset, gating_strategy = GatingTable)
plot(gatingset)

# Load in downsampling code
RFolder <- file.path("R")
MyFunctions <- list.files(RFolder, full.names=TRUE)
purrr::walk(.x=MyFunctions, .f=source)

# Downsample to include only Bcells population and export as new .fcs file
purrr::map(.x=gatingset[1], subset="Bcells", .f=Downsampling, DownsampleCount=2500, addon="CD20",
  returnType="fcs", StorageLocation="data/homework")
```

## Note for future:
Downsampling generated a new fcs file with 2500 B cells however, when interrogating the plots the gating of the B cells is incorrect and includes CD20- cells. Used own data that needs to be scaled properly prior to gating to ensure correct gtes can be applied.

# Problem 2
In the example for Downsampling() we only changed one keyword (GUID), after substituting in our desired addon right before the .fcs. Since keyword use might vary by manufacturer, create a couple additional arguments for Downsampling() that allow you to change out the values for some additional keywords.

```{r}

# Identify .fcs file keywords (Sony ID7000 used for acquisition)
flowFrame <- cytoset[[1, returnType = "flowFrame"]]
fcsDescription <- as.data.frame(keyword(flowFrame), check.names = FALSE)


# Option 1: Change addon to $FIL (Filename)

#' This function downsamples from a designated gate to our desired number
#' of cells, returning as a new .fcs file
#' 
#' @param x A GatingSet object, typically iterated in.
#' @param subset The gate from which to retrieve cell counts from 
#' @param inverse.transform Whether to revert values back to their
#' original untransformed values before export as an .fcs file, default
#' is set to TRUE
#' @param DownsampleCount The desired number of cells to downsample from
#' each gated population. If value is less than 1, subsets out the 
#' equivalent proportion from that specimen
#' @param addon An additional character value to add before .fcs in the FIL
#' keyword to tell the downsampled file apart from the original. 
#' @param StorageLocation A file.path to the folder you want to store the new downsampled
#' fcs file to. Default NULL results in .fcs file being stored in current working directory
#' @param returnType Whether to return as a "fcs" file (default), or "flowFrame" or "data.frame"
#' 
#' @importFrom flowWorkspace gs_pop_get_data
#' @importFrom flowCore parameters keyword write.FCS
#' @importFrom Biobase exprs
#' @importFrom dplyr slice_sample
#'  
#' 
Downsampling <- function(x, subset, inverse.transform=TRUE, DownsampleCount,
  addon, StorageLocation=NULL, returnType="fcs"){
  EventsInTheGate <- flowWorkspace::gs_pop_get_data(x, subset,
   inverse.transform=inverse.transform)
  MeasurementData <- Biobase::exprs(EventsInTheGate[[1]])
  MeasurementDataFramed <- as.data.frame(MeasurementData, check.names = FALSE)

  if (DownsampleCount < 1) {
      Count <- nrow(EventsInTheGate) # Original Count
      Count <- as.numeric(Count) #Sanity Check on Value Type
      Count <- Count*DownsampleCount # Target Cells
      Count <- round(Count, 0)
      DownsampleCount <- Count # Over-writting DownsampleCount used for downsampling
    }

  Downsampled_DataFrame <- dplyr::slice_sample(MeasurementDataFramed, n = DownsampleCount, replace = FALSE)

  DownsampledMatrix <- as.matrix(Downsampled_DataFrame)

  flowFrame <- EventsInTheGate[[1, returnType = "flowFrame"]]
  OriginalParameters <- flowCore::parameters(flowFrame)
  OriginalDescription <- flowCore::keyword(flowFrame)

  OriginalName <- OriginalDescription$`$FIL`
  UpdatedName <- paste0("_", addon, ".fcs")
  UpdatedFIL <- sub(".fcs", UpdatedName, OriginalName) #Swtiching out .fcs for Updated Name via the sub function
  OriginalDescription$`$FIL` <- UpdatedFIL

  NewFCS <- new("flowFrame", exprs=DownsampledMatrix, parameters=OriginalParameters, description=OriginalDescription)

  if (is.null(StorageLocation)){StorageLocation <- getwd()}

  StoreFCSFileHere <- file.path(StorageLocation, UpdatedFIL)
  
  if (returnType == "fcs"){
    flowCore::write.FCS(NewFCS, filename = StoreFCSFileHere, delimiter="#") # Write out .fcs file
  } else if (returnType == "data.frame"){
    return(Downsampled_DataFrame) #Return data.frame without metadata
  } else {
    return(NewFCS) #All other criterias return a flowFrame with metadata
    }

}

# Export new .fcs file with updated addon
purrr::map(.x=gatingset[1], subset="Bcells", .f=Downsampling, DownsampleCount=2500, addon="FILChange",
  returnType="fcs", StorageLocation="data/homework")

# Option 2: Add a NewName parameter that replaces original $FIL descriptor

#' This function downsamples from a designated gate to our desired number
#' of cells, returning as a new .fcs file
#' 
#' @param x A GatingSet object, typically iterated in.
#' @param subset The gate from which to retrieve cell counts from 
#' @param inverse.transform Whether to revert values back to their
#' original untransformed values before export as an .fcs file, default
#' is set to TRUE
#' @param DownsampleCount The desired number of cells to downsample from
#' each gated population. If value is less than 1, subsets out the 
#' equivalent proportion from that specimen
#' @param StorageLocation A file.path to the folder you want to store the new downsampled
#' fcs file to. Default NULL results in .fcs file being stored in current working directory
#' @param returnType Whether to return as a "fcs" file (default), or "flowFrame" or "data.frame"
#' @param NewName Changes sample name by replaceing $FIL descriptor to distinguish
#' downsampled files apart from original. 
#' 
#' @importFrom flowWorkspace gs_pop_get_data
#' @importFrom flowCore parameters keyword write.FCS
#' @importFrom Biobase exprs
#' @importFrom dplyr slice_sample
#'  
#' 
Downsampling <- function(x, subset, inverse.transform=TRUE, DownsampleCount,
StorageLocation=NULL, returnType="fcs", NewName){
  EventsInTheGate <- flowWorkspace::gs_pop_get_data(x, subset,
   inverse.transform=inverse.transform)
  MeasurementData <- Biobase::exprs(EventsInTheGate[[1]])
  MeasurementDataFramed <- as.data.frame(MeasurementData, check.names = FALSE)

  if (DownsampleCount < 1) {
      Count <- nrow(EventsInTheGate) # Original Count
      Count <- as.numeric(Count) #Sanity Check on Value Type
      Count <- Count*DownsampleCount # Target Cells
      Count <- round(Count, 0)
      DownsampleCount <- Count # Over-writting DownsampleCount used for downsampling
    }

  Downsampled_DataFrame <- dplyr::slice_sample(MeasurementDataFramed, n = DownsampleCount, replace = FALSE)

  DownsampledMatrix <- as.matrix(Downsampled_DataFrame)

  flowFrame <- EventsInTheGate[[1, returnType = "flowFrame"]]
  OriginalParameters <- flowCore::parameters(flowFrame)
  OriginalDescription <- flowCore::keyword(flowFrame)

  OriginalName <- OriginalDescription$`$FIL`
  UpdatedName <- paste0(NewName, "_", ".fcs")
  UpdatedFIL <- sub(OriginalName, UpdatedName, OriginalName) #Swtiching out original name for new name
  OriginalDescription$`$FIL` <- UpdatedFIL

  NewFCS <- new("flowFrame", exprs=DownsampledMatrix, parameters=OriginalParameters, description=OriginalDescription)

  if (is.null(StorageLocation)){StorageLocation <- getwd()}

  StoreFCSFileHere <- file.path(StorageLocation, UpdatedFIL)
  
  if (returnType == "fcs"){
    flowCore::write.FCS(NewFCS, filename = StoreFCSFileHere, delimiter="#") # Write out .fcs file
  } else if (returnType == "data.frame"){
    return(Downsampled_DataFrame) #Return data.frame without metadata
  } else {
    return(NewFCS) #All other criterias return a flowFrame with metadata
    }

}

# Export new .fcs file with replacement name
purrr::map(.x=gatingset[1], subset="Bcells", .f=Downsampling, DownsampleCount=2500, NewName="Rh_PBMC_CD20Downsample",
  returnType="fcs", StorageLocation="data/homework")
```

# Problem 3
Trickier - After concatenating out an .fcs file for a cell subset of your choice, reload it back into R, extract out both the exprs matrix, and the description list. Using the keywords that got added, figure out a way using dplyr to revert the numeric keys (denoted by “_key”) in the exprs matrix back to their original character values as recorded in the keywords.

```{r}
# Load in Cytonmetry in R saved gatingset
FolderandName <- file.path("data", "SFCGatingSet.gs")
SFCgatingset <- load_gs(FolderandName)
plot(SFCgatingset)

# Load Concatenate function
RFolder <- file.path("R")
MyFunctions <- list.files(RFolder, full.names=TRUE)
purrr::walk(.x=MyFunctions, .f=source)

# Update metadata
CurrentMetadata <-pData(SFCgatingset)
CurrentMetadata

MetadataCSV <- list.files("data", pattern = ".csv", full.names = TRUE)
AdditionalMetadata <- read.csv(MetadataCSV, check.names = FALSE)
colnames(CurrentMetadata)
colnames(AdditionalMetadata)

UpdatedMetadata <- left_join(CurrentMetadata, AdditionalMetadata, "name")
rownames(UpdatedMetadata) <- UpdatedMetadata$name
pData(SFCgatingset) <- UpdatedMetadata
pData(SFCgatingset)

# Concatenate CD4 population from gatingset and export as .fcs file
Concatenate(gs=SFCgatingset, subset="CD4+", addon="CD4", DownsampleCount=2000,
  desiredCols=c("name", "condition", "infant_sex", "HEU_status"), returnType="fcs",
  filename="ConcatenatedCD4")

# Load in concatenated CD4 .fcs file to flowFrame
library(flowCore)
ConcatFile <- list.files(pattern = "ConcatenatedCD4.fcs", full.names = TRUE)
ConcatflowFrame <- read.FCS(ConcatFile, truncate_max_range = FALSE, transformation = FALSE)
ConcatflowFrame

# Extract Description list and exprs matrix
DescriptionList <- ConcatflowFrame@description
ConcatMatrix <- ConcatflowFrame@exprs

# Explore dplyr vignette 'Recoding columns and replacing values'
browseVignettes(package = "dplyr")

# Revert the numeric keys in the exprs matrix back to their original character values as recorded in the keywords
colnames(ConcatMatrix)

ConcatDF <- as.data.frame(ConcatMatrix, check.names = FALSE)
ConcatDFUpdated <- ConcatDF |> 
  mutate(infant_sex = recode(
    as.character(infant_sex), "1000" = "Male", "2000" = "Female")) |>
      mutate(HEU_status = recode(
        as.character(HEU_status), "1000" = "HEU-hi", "2000" = "HEU-lo", "3000" = "HU" )) |>
          mutate(condition = recode(
            as.character(condition), "1000" = "Ctrl")) |>
              mutate(name = recode(
                as.character(name), "1000" = "2025_07_26_AB_02-INF052-00_Ctrl_Unmixed__Tcells.fcs", 
                "2000" = "2025_07_26_AB_02-INF100-00_Ctrl_Unmixed__Tcells.fcs", 
                "3000" = "2025_07_26_AB_02-INF179-00_Ctrl_Unmixed__Tcells.fcs"
              ))
```
